problem: Semantic 3D mapping pipelines, especially the widely used Recursive Bayesian Update (RBU) fusion, produce highly overconfident voxel labels even when the 2D segmentation model is reasonably calibrated; map calibration had not been systematically studied.
motivation: Calibrated uncertainty allows more cautious decisions in robotics, and downstream agents such as ObjectNav rely on semantic maps. The observation is that 2D calibration barely changes voxel calibration, so the fusion stage itself (independence assumption, outlier sensitivity, viewpoint bias) must be addressed.
key_idea: Treat the whole fusion pipeline as the object to calibrate, and learn a unified, differentiable fusion (GLFS) that combines gated fusion type, logit temperature or vector scaling and learned sample weights, optimized for 3D map calibration and accuracy.
insight: 2D temperature scaling improves pixel mECE but leaves voxel mECE almost unchanged (Segformer 0.451 to 0.450), whereas 3D temperature scaling cuts voxel mECE to 0.176, so calibration must be optimized at the map level. Averaging-based fusion is a strong baseline, and vector scaling often hurts accuracy. The learned GLFS improves calibration without losing mIoU. In ObjectNav, fusion helps mainly by being robust to outlying predictions.
method: Overconfidence analysis: identifies causes of fusion overconfidence (uncalibrated 2D model, incorrect independence/double counting, outlier sensitivity, viewpoint coverage and density bias, metric mapping errors).
mECE metric: class-frequency-agnostic calibration error that bins by confidence and ground-truth class, then averages across classes; also reports TL-ECE and Brier.
Alternative fusion strategies: histogram voting, naive averaging, geometric mean, compared against RBU.
3D Temperature/Vector scaling: logit scaling parameters tau are optimized (Bayesian optimization) to minimize mECE on the fused voxels instead of on image pixels.

GLFS: a unified fusion formula with gates G and epsilon interpolating between RBU, geometric mean, naive averaging and histogram, plus learnable temperature and a look-up-table sample weight indexed by predicted class, distance and incidence angle.
GLFS loss: eta*mDECE (a differentiable mECE analogue) + NLL, trained by backprop with voxel caching, real-time capable in Open3D GPU dense SLAM.
ObjectNav integration: the fused 3D semantic point cloud is projected into a 2D semantic map for PEANUT, with detection by thresholding the fused map and keeping the largest goal connected component.

setting.backbone: Segformer-b4 and ESANet (fine-tuned on ScanNet) for mapping; Segformer fine-tuned on HM3D for the ObjectNav agent; PEANUT goal prediction network (not fine-tuned)
setting.training_data: Segformer pretrained on ADE20K, ESANet on NYUv2, both fine-tuned on ScanNet 20 classes (every 30th frame of train); calibration parameters learned on 79 ScanNet val scans; ObjectNav Segformer fine-tuned on random-exploration images from HM3D v0.1
setting.action_space: PEANUT modular ObjectNav: predicted goal on 2D map with planner (discrete low-level actions)
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D) for ObjectNav; ScanNet for mapping
setting.privileged: ground-truth poses for mapping experiments; a GT segmentation ablation row for ObjectNav; none for main ObjectNav rows

numbers.eval_set_note: episodes 500-999 of the 2022 Habitat ObjectNav challenge validation set; hyperparameters tuned on the first 500
numbers.backbone: Segformer fine-tuned on HM3D + PEANUT goal network (not fine-tuned on fused maps)
numbers.extra: uses live 3D fusion; SSPL also reported (0.347)
numbers.evidence: Table II: Fusion-NA Segformer 0.312 SPL, 0.604 Success, 0.347 SSPL, 3.576 DTG

numbers.eval_set_note: episodes 500-999 of the 2022 Habitat ObjectNav challenge validation set
numbers.backbone: Segformer fine-tuned on HM3D + PEANUT goal network
numbers.evidence: Table II: Fusion-RBU Segformer 0.314 SPL, 0.596 Success, 0.351 SSPL, 3.549 DTG

numbers_note: Mapping calibration results on ScanNet (mECE, mIoU) for GLFS are only shown in figures, not tables; only the Table I 2D vs 3D temperature values are printed. The HM3D-ObjNav SR of the paper's own methods is printed as fractions and converted to percent.
results: On ScanNet, GLFS typically exceeds other fusion/calibration combos in accuracy or calibration without degrading mIoU, and RBU is among the worst calibrated. In ObjectNav, Fusion-NA reaches 0.604 success versus 0.596 for NDF and Fusion-RBU (Segformer), with both fusion variants at slightly higher SPL (0.312/0.314) than NDF (0.295); GT segmentation gives 0.724.
limitations: Downstream ObjectNav gains are small (0.596 to 0.604 SR, within standard error), and PEANUT was not fine-tuned on the new fused maps.
Calibration evaluated only on ScanNet with two segmentation models and GT poses, with mapping calibration results given mostly in figures.
Naive averaging needs more evidence before targets are detected, slightly hurting SPL; ESANet was harder to calibrate.
